title: Support of a finite type quasi-coherent module and of its pullback
statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] on a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], with stalks $\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], residue fields $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and support $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)=\{x:\mathcal F_x
eq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is closed in $X$. (2) For $x\in X$: $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\iff\mathcal F_x
e0\iff\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)
e0$. (3) For every morphism of schemes $f:Y	o X$ the pullback $f^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is of finite type and $\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F)$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (part (1)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed], applied to the quasi-coherent finite type module $\mathcal F$, $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ is a closed subset of $X$. (Stacks deduces (1) from Modules 01BA, or from 056I, 01PB and 00L2; the cited node carries the second route.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: part (1), via Modules Lemma 01BA (modules-lemma-support-finite-type-closed)

proof.text: *Step 2 (first equivalence of (2)).* $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\iff\mathcal F_x\neq0$ is the definition of the support [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: 'The first equivalence in (2) is the definition of support'

proof.text: *Step 3 ($\mathcal F_x$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module).* Let $x\in X$ and choose an affine open $U\ni x$ [def-pc-scheme], $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] $M$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, say by $m_1,\dots,m_r$, and there is an $A$-linear isomorphism $M_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong\mathcal F_x$ compatible with the ring isomorphism $A_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (its Step 3). Every element of $M_{\mathfrak p_x}$ is $m/s=\sum_i(a_i/s)(m_i/1)$, so $m_1/1,\dots,m_r/1$ generate $M_{\mathfrak p_x}$ over $A_{\mathfrak p_x}$, and their images generate $\mathcal F_x$ over $\mathcal O_{X,x}$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: implicit in the appeal to Nakayama's lemma for (2): $\mathcal F_x$ must be a finite $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Step 4 (second equivalence of (2), Nakayama).* $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field]; $\mathcal F_x$ is finitely generated (Step 3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to $M=\mathcal F_x$ and the empty family ($r=0$), in its tensor form: the empty family generates $\mathcal F_x$ (i.e. $\mathcal F_x=0$) if and only if it generates $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x\cong\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)$ (i.e. that module is $0$). Hence $\mathcal F_x\neq0\iff\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)\neq0$. With Step 2 this proves (2).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: 'the second equivalence follows from Nakayama's lemma, see Algebra, Lemma 00DV (algebra-lemma-NAK)'

proof.text: *Step 5 ($f^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type).* Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes. $f^*\mathcal F$ is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type] and quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. This is the first claim of (3), and it allows applying (2) (Steps 2--4) to $f^*\mathcal F$ on $Y$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: '$f^*\mathcal F$ is of finite type by Modules, Lemma 01B6'; quasi-coherence (Modules, Lemma 01BG), needed to apply (2) to $f^*\mathcal F$, is left implicit in the source

proof.text: *Step 6 (the fibre of the pullback).* Let $y\in Y$, $x=f(y)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\varphi=f^\sharp_y:A\to B$, a local homomorphism since $f$ is a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], so $\varphi(\mathfrak m_x)\subseteq\mathfrak m_y$ and $\varphi$ induces the field map $\bar\varphi:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] $(f^*\mathcal F)_y\cong\mathcal F_x\otimes_AB$ as $B$-modules. Hence, by associativity of the tensor product and $B\otimes_B\kappa(y)=\kappa(y)$, $(f^*\mathcal F)_y\otimes_B\kappa(y)\cong\mathcal F_x\otimes_A\kappa(y)$, where $\kappa(y)$ is an $A$-algebra through $A\to B\to\kappa(y)$; this map factors as $A\to\kappa(x)\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi}\kappa(y)$, so again by associativity $\mathcal F_x\otimes_A\kappa(y)\cong(\mathcal F_x\otimes_A\kappa(x))\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: '$(f^*\mathcal F)_y=\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, see Sheaves, Lemma 0098 (sheaves-lemma-stalk-pullback-modules)'

proof.text:
*Step 7 (extension of scalars along a field extension).* Let $V=\mathcal F_x\otimes_A\kappa(x)$, a $\kappa(x)$-vector space with a basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$. Then $V\otimes_{\kappa(x)}\kappa(y)\cong\kappa(y)^{(I)}$, which is nonzero iff $I
eq\emptyset$ iff $V
eq0$. With Step 6: $(f^*\mathcal F)_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y,y}}\kappa(y)
eq0\iff\mathcal F_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\kappa(x)
eq0$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: 'Hence $(f^*\mathcal F)_y\otimes\kappa(y)$ is nonzero if and only if $\mathcal F_x\otimes\kappa(x)$ is nonzero'

proof.text: *Step 8 (conclusion of (3)).* By (2) for $f^*\mathcal F$ on $Y$ (Steps 2--4, applicable by Step 5), $y\in\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)\iff(f^*\mathcal F)_y\otimes\kappa(y)\neq0$; by Step 7 this holds iff $\mathcal F_{f(y)}\otimes\kappa(f(y))\neq0$, which by (2) for $\mathcal F$ holds iff $f(y)\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$. So $\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)=f^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type), proof: 'By (2) this implies $x\in\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$ iff $y\in\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)$'

proof_origin.place: Morphisms of Schemes, Lemma 056J (lemma-support-finite-type) and its proof

lean.statement: theorem finiteType_module_support_pullback {X : Scheme.{u}} (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] : IsClosed {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ∧ (∀ x : X, ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x) ↔ ¬ Subsingleton (residueFiber F x)) ∧ ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ X), ((tensorPullback f).obj F).IsFiniteType ∧ {y : Y | ¬ Subsingleton (((tensorPullback f).obj F).presheaf.stalk y)} = f.base ⁻¹' {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)}
